reason: Conversation 2 was efficient and safe: it asked the right power-supply questions in one pass, explicitly warned against live testing or removing panels, and escalated to an engineer without naming a part, though it did lean prematurely toward 'mains input or control board' and never raised the spur fuse or door latch. Conversation 1 repeatedly ignored what the homeowner said (asking to check a plug after being told it's hard-wired, inventing a 'dedicated breaker'), suggested multimeter/live voltage testing against the safety boundary, and finished with an impractical instruction to plug a lamp into a fused spur that has no socket, leaving the customer frustrated. Both missed the sensible 'try a known-good spur fuse' step, but Conversation 2 reached an appropriate engineer escalation cleanly while Conversation 1 wasted several turns and gave unsafe or unusable advice.
